The pronunciation of 你 was similar to 尔 in old Chinese, but they no longer sound similar in modern Mandarin due to historical phonetic changes. 尔 also serves as a meaning component.

好.notes: It is good (好) for a woman (女) and her child (子) to be together.

我.notes: Pictograph of a weapon or farming tool with a forked blade and long handle. The meaning "I; me" is a phonetic loan.

学.notes:
Simplified form of 學.  Originally composed of the numbers five (㐅) and six (六), representing study of arithmetic. 
Later two hands (又) were added on the left and right side of the character, possibly depicting counting with fingers or hands-on teaching.
Finally a child (子) was added to the bottom, depicting a child being educated.
The bottom part of 六 (six) was reanalyzed as 宀 (roof) and interpreted as a building for learning.

components.hint: Shorthand form of the 㐅 (five), 六 (six), and 又 (hand) components in the top part of the traditional character 學.

生.notes: Pictograph of a sprout emerging from the ground.

六.notes: Originally a pictograph of a tent or building. Unrelated to modern meaning.

且.notes: Originally a pictograph of a sacrificial altar. The current meaning "moreover" is a phonetic loan.

朱.notes: Based on the original meaning "tree trunk", now written as 株. Derivative of 木 (tree). The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

definitions: non-Han people, esp. to the East of China
夷.notes: Origin unclear. Possibly depicts a string around a bow.

冄.notes: 冄 is a component form of 冉.

definitions: to walk (side part of split character)
辶.notes: 辶 is a component form of 辵.

definitions: one of the eight ancient musical instruments 八音[bā​yīn]
土.notes: Pictograph of a lump of clay on a pottery wheel.

卜.notes: Pictograph of a crack on a bone. In ancient China such cracks were used for divination.

自.notes: Pictograph of a nose. Original form of 鼻 (nose). In China, when people point to themselves, they typically point to their nose.

definitions: third of the ten Heavenly Stems 十天干[shí​tiān​gān]
letter "C" or Roman "III" in list "A, B, C", or "I, II, III" etc
丙.notes: Origin unclear. Variously explained as a table or pedestal, or a fish tail.

力.notes: Pictograph of a plow, representing strength

止.notes: Pictograph of a foot. The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "stop".

definitions: eighth of the ten Heavenly Stems 十天干[shí​tiān​gān]
letter "H" or Roman "VIII" in list "A, B, C", or "I, II, III" etc
辛.notes: Pictograph of a chisel-like tool used to tattoo the face of criminals as punishment (see 黑).

昜.notes: Pictograph of rays of light coming from the sun. Based on the original meaning "sunshine", now written as 暘. The meaning later shifted to "bright" and "expansive".

components.hint: Depicts rays of sunshine.

景.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 日 represents the meaning and 京 represents the sound.

食.notes: Pictograph of food being spooned into the mouth. Not related to 良.

广.notes: Variant form of 宀 (roof). In simplified Chinese 广 is also used to mean "wide", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 廣.

definitions: fourth of the ten Heavenly Stems 十天干[shí​tiān​gān]
letter "D" or Roman "IV" in list "A, B, C", or "I, II, III" etc
丁.notes: Pictograph of a nail, which is now written as 釘.

definitions: 10th earthly branch: 5-7 p.m., 8th solar month (8th September-7th October), year of the Rooster
酉.notes: Pictograph of a container for wine.

components.hint: Seems to depict an arrow in a container.
The purpose of this component is unclear.

先.notes: Depicts a person (人) stepping forward (止) leading the way.

definitions: classifier for lessons, subjects, branches of technology
门.notes: Simplified form of 門.  Pictograph of a gate.

definitions: see also 冬字頭|冬字头[dōng​zì​tóu]
夂.notes: 夂 is a component form of 止.

definitions: "to eat" or "food" radical in Chinese characters (Kangxi radical 184)
饣.notes: 饣 is a component form of 食.

definitions: abbr. for 反切[fǎn​qiè] phonetic system
反.notes: Pictograph of a hand (又) climbing a cliff (厂). Based on original meaning "pull", later extended to "turn around", "oppose".

耂.notes: 耂 is a component form of 老.

交.originalMeaning: intersect; cross; hand over; make friends
交.notes: Pictograph of a person standing with crossed legs, conveying the meaning "to cross".

components.hint: The purpose of this component is unclear.
The purpose of this component is unclear.

臤.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 又 represents the meaning and 臣 represents the sound.

components.hint: The pronunciation of 臤 was similar to 臣 in old Chinese, but they no longer sound similar in modern Mandarin due to historical phonetic changes.

巾.notes: Pictograph of a cloth hanging downwards.

敝.notes: Depicts shabby clothes that have been beaten down.

components.hint: Depicts ruined clothes.
攵 is a component form of 攴.

钅.notes: 钅 is a component form of 金.

纟.notes: 纟 is a component form of 糸.

氏.notes: Pictograph of a man bowing down.

白.notes: Origin unclear. Used in ancient texts to mean "white" and "hundred" (百).

立.notes: Pictograph of a person standing on the ground.

𤣩.notes: 𤣩 is a component form of 玉.

元.notes: Pictograph of a person with two lines added at the head area, representing the meaning the meaning "head" or "first".

曰.notes: Pictograph of a line, representing speech, coming out of a mouth (口).

components.hint: Represents a line of speech coming out of the mouth.

匃.notes: Variant form of 丐. Origin unclear. Possibly depicts a beggar holding his hand out.

definitions: algebraic term for a large number (old)
京.notes: Pictograph of a tall building. Similar to 高. Based on the original meaning "high place". The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "capital city".

definitions: Kangxi radical 79, occurring in 段, 毅, 殺 etc
殳.notes: Pictograph of a hand holding a spear.

components.hint: Depicts a spear.
Depicts a hand.

厂.notes: Pictograph of a cliff or similarly shaped object. In simplified Chinese 厂 is also used to mean "factory", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 廠. In simplified characters the 广 component is often written as 厂.

比.notes: Pictograph of two people side-by-side, conveying the meaning "to put together", "match", or "compare".

definitions: state official or subject in dynastic China
I, your servant (used in addressing the sovereign)
臣.notes: Pictograph of an eye, similar to 目. Based on the original meaning "to glare at", now written as 瞋. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

攵.notes: 攵 is a component form of 攴.
